alt_audio_surface_label: Example alternate-audio posture for official voter-information media routes
delivery_role_note: The service reviews alternate spoken tracks over already-open official media so dubbed, descriptive, commentary, or other player-native audio layers remain subordinate to the full recording plus the current official page/help lane rather than quietly becoming a shadow spoken edition.

reviewed_alt_audio_contexts.context_note: Reviewed whether the player exposes original audio plus one or more dubbed language tracks and whether those tracks are clearly labeled for viewers.
Reviewed whether any spoken track is auto-generated, whether its limitations are treated honestly, and whether the current written route remains recoverable when the track is partial or doubtful.
Reviewed whether descriptive or commentary tracks exist and whether those accessibility or context layers stay distinct from controlling operational guidance.
Reviewed whether a voter can recover the full recording date/scope and the current written help lane after changing the audio track.

track_provenance_note: The service distinguishes original audio, uploaded dubs, automatic dubs, descriptive audio, and commentary rather than treating every spoken track as the same review state.
language_and_review_note: Alternate spoken tracks do not by themselves prove that the office reviewed or currently stands behind that exact wording as an equivalent official translation.
current_help_recovery_note: When the spoken track is stale, partial, or ambiguous, the route points back to the current official page, reviewed FAQ/help entry, or named office contact instead of treating the selected audio track as controlling.
portability_note: Audio-track switching is treated as playback state rather than as a durable portable current edition of the answer.
